_doc: Per-edition decisions for usj_source.py's opt-in bracket/paren text-stripping. DEFAULT IS NO STRIPPING — an edition not listed here (or with a field omitted) gets its raw verse text, brackets and parens included, exactly as ingested; nothing is ever removed automatically. A rule should only be added here after a human has reviewed that edition's entry in config/text_strip_report.md (generated by `pipeline/scripts/text_strip_candidates.py`, or `make text-strip-report`) and is confident the flagged spans are genuine editorial/apparatus noise, not real translated or supplied content. Keyed by the edition tag as it appears in the ingest-cache dir name (pipeline/work/ingest-cache/usj-<tag>/...). Fields: strip_brackets (bool) — blanket-remove every [...] span; only sane when an edition uses [...] consistently for ONE purpose (e.g. long-form editorial commentary). Do NOT set this for an edition that uses [...] for supplied/added words (e.g. Young's Literal Translation-style editions) — that bracketed text is real translation content, not a note. strip_parens_noise (bool) — run usj_source._paren_is_noise's discriminating classifier over (...) spans (source-language citations, verse/book cross-references, 'ordagrant'/'betyder' metalinguistic glosses, f.Kr./e.Kr. era annotations) and drop only spans matching one of those patterns; everything else in parens is kept as real content (short alternate/amplified glosses are legitimate per docs/publishing-principles.md #4, not noise). reason (string, required alongside either flag) — the evidence that justified the decision, so a later reviewer doesn't have to re-derive it.

swk.reason: Svenska Kärnbibeln ('en expanderad översättning'). [...] is used exclusively for long-form editorial/study-note commentary inline in verse text — full-corpus sample: avg 18.7 words/span, up to 894 words in one span, often longer than the verse's own translated sentence; left unstripped this floods eflomal/gloss with non-scripture prose (measured: swk gap-fill precision collapsed to ~0.5-0.7% before this was found). (...) is a heterogeneous mix in the SAME edition: ~83% are short (one to a few words) alternate/amplified Swedish glosses that are genuine translated content worth aligning (e.g. '(blygdes)', '(oförtjänt kärlek, god favör)'), ~17% are real noise — source-language citations ('hebr. chesed', 'gr. logos'), cross-references ('1 Mos 1:1', 'vers 17'), metalinguistic glosses ('ordagrant ...', '... betyder ...'), era/date annotations ('735-715 f.Kr.'). Verified via full-corpus sweep across all 182 cached editions (the noise-pattern regexes are Swedish-lexical, checked they don't misfire on other languages' legitimate parenthetical scripture text) plus a controlled before/after benchmark A/B (git stash isolating the code change as the only variable): discriminating paren strip alone gave a small, consistent, non-regressive improvement (eflomal-Hebrew 67.6%->68.2%, gloss-Greek 75.2%->75.8%).
